# Victim in Brock Turner Stanford sexual assault case goes public with her name and memoir

Chanel Miller, once known as "Jane Doe," titled her book "Know My Name."

1:38

Chanel Miller's rape case became U.S. news in 2016 when she read a statement at the sentencing of Brock Turner. Turner, a Stanford student, was convicted in the assault but given just six months in jail.

Mariah Tiffany

By [Enjoli Francis](https://abcnews.com/author/enjoli_francis)

September 4, 2019, 4:24 PM

Share

The woman who [Brock Turner was convicted](https://abcnews.com/US/sex-assault-law-inspired-brock-turners-stanford-case/story?id=41740934) of sexually assaulting in 2016 has come forward, not only revealing her real name but also releasing a new memoir.

In the book titled "Know My Name," which she began working on in 2017, Chanel Miller discusses the [assault](https://abcnews.com/US/textbook-showing-brock-turners-mug-shot-section-rape/story?id=49845886) , which occurred after a [fraternity party](https://abcnews.com/US/anti-hazing-law-named-penn-state-fraternity-pledge/story?id=58609422) in 2015, [The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2019/09/04/books/chanel-miller-brock-turner-assault-stanford.html) reported.

...

I had to force myself to relearn my real name, my identity, to relearn that this is not all that I am, that I am not just a drunk victim at a frat party found behind a dumpster.
